title: A parallel-coupled stripline section: two 2.33 mm strips 0.18 mm apart beside each other over 8.72 mm, each running on to a port at its own end of the box and ending open at the other, midway between planes 4 mm apart in PTFE (εr = 2.2): S21 against the open-circuited coupled section's line theory, a quarter wavelength long at 5 GHz
source: The open-circuited coupled section (each line open at one end, the band-pass section): Z11 = Z22 = −j(Z0e + Z0o)/2 cot θ, Z12 = −j(Z0e − Z0o)/2 csc θ (E. M. T. Jones, J. T. Bolljahn, Coupled-strip-transmission-line filters and directional couplers, IRE Trans. MTT 4(2):75–81, 1956; D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 2012, §8.7, Table 8.8): at θ = π/2 an inverter K = (Z0e − Z0o)/2, |S21| = 2KZ/(K² + Z²), set by the coupling C = (Z0e − Z0o)/(Z0e + Z0o) = 0.3387 (−9.40 dB). Z0e = 77.13 Ω, Z0o = 38.10 Ω by Cohn's coupled-strip mapping (IRE Trans. MTT 3(5):29–38, 1955), the feeds and the ports' reference Z = 62.21 Ω by his stripline (IRE Trans. MTT 2(2):52–57, 1954); TEM in one dielectric, θ = β(ℓ + 2Δ): each strip's open end lies beside the other strip, which runs on, so its extension Δ adds to the coupled length at both ends (0.692 mm, the middle of the open end's bracket as in stripline-ends), and the feeds before and after are as much shorter. Evaluated by emcraft-theory::coupled, apart from the solver
